ironclad.objective: Defeat Kin Priest with HP left. Its Minions abandon when the leader dies; damage to a follower is only worthwhile if killing it prevents enough repeated incoming damage.
ironclad.resources: Use Dexterity Potion at entry before blocks. Hold Blood Potion until at least 16 HP missing, or use immediately if death is otherwise possible. No conservation bonus for dying with a potion.
ironclad.tactics: The deck has upgraded Bludgeon (42), Bash (3 Vulnerable), Setup Strike (+4 temporary Strength) and defensive Flame Barrier/Armaments/Iron Wave. Seek a fast leader kill rather than spending both Bludgeons on full-health followers. A follower with a feasible immediate kill and large repeated attacks can be removed. Bash the leader before subsequent attacks, sustain Vulnerable through future Bludgeon turns. Setup Strike before other damage. Armaments upgrades ALL remaining hand cards, but do not spend its energy if it prevents a much stronger three-cost Bludgeon. Headbutt topdecks based on the next turn: Bludgeon while leader is vulnerable, Bash to enable future burst, or Flame Barrier before high incoming. At entry Bludgeon Priest is a reasonable tempo play; 14 incoming is partly covered by Plating. Plating supplies end-turn block. Defend against large attacks, but excessive block with no progress loses to scaling. Flame Barrier retaliation affects every hit. Recompute threats after each action; do not assume a planned target survives or a card stays at its index.
ironclad.expiry: First actual Boss reward or defeat; card selection caused by a card or potion remains inside combat.
ironclad.invalidation: Unexpected mechanic, unknown target effect, lethal forecast, or inability to achieve leader progress. This fixed-plan arm records the failure and continues Jev; no unbudgeted teacher rescue.

silent.objective: Defeat Kin Priest while avoiding a long fight with all three enemies alive. Leader death dismisses Minions.
silent.resources: Dexterity Potion immediately before any block. Poison Potion on Kin Priest immediately to gain all damage ticks and combine with Poisoned Stab. Use rather than finish defeated with potions.
silent.tactics: Poisoned Stab repeatedly on Priest gives damage between turns. Prefer leader focus unless an attacking follower can be killed cheaply and promptly. Neutralize the largest attack source (often Priest), preferably before attacks change intent. Backstab and upgraded Strikes supply tempo. Flechettes benefits from Skills in hand: inspect hit count and play it BEFORE spending those Skills. Dexterity plus Backflip/Survivor/Cloak and Dagger/Dodge and Roll sustain defense. Dodge and Roll has next-turn block value; Backflip can find poison and damage, but spend energy with subsequent plays in mind. Count Plating at turn end and avoid excess block when the leader is close to dead. Survivor should discard an unplayable or unusable card, preserving useful zero-cost attacks. Newly created Shivs need fresh indices. Shadow Step's printed rules and current stats are authoritative; do not invent an effect from its name. Use HP as a finite resource to finish the Priest before enemy damage escalates.
silent.expiry: First actual Boss reward or defeat; in-combat card selections do not expire the plan.
silent.invalidation: Unexpected mechanic, lethal forecast, or stalled poison/damage. This fixed-plan arm continues Jev without extra rescue.
